name: Asherman Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Hysteroscopic Diagnostic Criteria for Asherman Syndrome

criteria.description: Visualization of intrauterine adhesions or synechiae by hysteroscopy
History of hypomenorrhea or amenorrhea following uterine trauma or surgery
Findings consistent with intrauterine adhesions on imaging modalities such as hysterosalpingography or sonohysterography

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of intrauterine adhesions confirmed by hysteroscopy combined with clinical history of menstrual disturbance post uterine trauma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily confirmed by direct visualization via hysteroscopy; imaging and clinical history support diagnosis.

imaging: Hysterosalpingography showing filling defects or obliteration of uterine cavity
Hysteroscopic visualization of fibrous adhesions within the uterine cavity
other: History of uterine trauma such as dilation and curettage, cesarean section, or uterine surgery

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of intrauterine adhesions on hysteroscopy
Atrophic endometrium with thin lining on ultrasound
Presence of endometrial inflammation on biopsy
May present with abnormal uterine bleeding but preserved menstrual flow

redFlags: Recurrent pregnancy loss with history of uterine surgery
Severe hypomenorrhea or absence of menstruation in reproductive-aged female
references: March CM. Asherman's syndrome. Semin Reprod Med. 2011;29(3):233-44.
American Society for Reproductive Medicine. Practice Committee guidelines on intrauterine adhesions.
